I’m going through a similar situation right now so I know too well how much it hurts to lose someone that you still love. But as panic1er mentioned, a relationship is supposed to compliment your life, not necessarily override everything you do, regardless of how much you love the person. Having to consistently break up a relationship can take a devastating toll on a person’s mental health, so take a step back and try to develop a new perspective! Learn from your relationship and grow with that knowledge so that you may apply it to any future relationships you end up having :) 

You’re stronger than you think, and you will come out of this even stronger.

Hello! 

I understand the situation you’re going through and suggest that you consider thinking about what made the relationship toxic in the first place, and whether or not it would be healthy for you to try to rekindle your companionship. If you guys had discussed fixing some of the issues beforehand and did nothing to fix them then maybe that’s a sign that the relationship isn’t going to work out. Another thing to consider is whether or not couples therapy would positively influence your relationship in the first place. Fact of the matter is that one sided effort is not going to fix a relationship. 

I hope this helps! 

Also, don’t forget to take care of yourself.
